newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet says Sirti sale time not set.
newsitem.headline: Stet says Sirti sale time not set.

text.p: Italian state-controlled telecoms holding Stet said on Thursday no time had yet been set for the sale of its cable-making unit Sirti.
Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said earlier that Stet, which is due to be privatised later this year after merging with its fixed-line operator Telecom Italia, would sell off the unit by the summer.
"Various hypotheses are still under consideration...thus no decision has yet been taken," Stet said in a brief statement.
Stet is due to put on the market its 48.9 percent stake in Sirti which is already quoted on the Milan bourse.
Il Sole had said Stet would also separately sell off its 50 percent stake in telecoms systems maker Italtel of which Germany's Siemens holds the rest.
But a longer time-frame was seen for that sale after plans to merge Sirti with Italtel appeared to have been dropped, it said.
Il Sole added that the Treasury, Stet's main shareholder, was also studying plans for the liquidation of Stet's heavy loss-making MMP advertising agency.
